technical_and_design_decisions: Treat U4 and U5 as duplicate requirements and implement one HDFS-backed custom-module uber-jar capability.
Use the Hadoop FileSystem abstraction for uber-jar storage and retrieval, allowing HDFS configuration and high-availability behavior to be supplied by the deployment environment.
Make the HDFS uber-jar location and YARN configuration location overrideable through existing CF/application configuration mechanisms, with backward-compatible defaults.
Use atomic or temporary-file-based HDFS writes followed by rename to reduce the risk of exposing incomplete uber-jars during failure scenarios.
Implement Spark job stopping through the existing Spark job or submission manager, preferring graceful termination and using the existing forceful termination mechanism when required.
Implement the RxJava feature as a configurable processor module using the RxJava version and threading conventions already present in the codebase.
Treat U2 as a design spike only: produce customer-use-case findings, an XD-runtime-compatible design, DSL/UI scope, and phased next steps rather than implementing ACL functionality.
Use profiling tools such as Java Flight Recorder, async-profiler, or an equivalent supported profiler to investigate startup CPU consumption for both admin and container servers.
Preserve existing local-filesystem behavior as the default where possible and add automated tests for configuration overrides, HDFS failures, job termination, and processor behavior.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Java 17-compatible Spring-based codebase with established build, test, logging, configuration, and deployment conventions.
Existing interfaces are available for custom-module installation, Spark job management, CF configuration, and server startup; no major platform refactoring is required.
HDFS and YARN client libraries are already available or can be added through normal dependency changes without resolving incompatible transitive dependencies.
The ACL story is explicitly limited to the requested spike scope and does not include production ACL enforcement, persistence, authentication integration, or UI implementation.
The performance investigation has access to representative admin and container server startup scenarios and can produce profiles without requiring production customer environments.
The requested Spark stop operation applies to jobs managed by the existing application and does not require changes to Spark itself or to external cluster schedulers.
No new public REST API, command-line interface, or user interface is required beyond existing extension points and configuration properties.
Documentation includes implementation notes, configuration references, profiling findings, design-spike output, and test evidence, but not a full end-user guide.

Effort represents one developer's work-hours, including coding, automated testing, investigation, documentation, and local integration verification; elapsed waiting time for external environments is excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module lifecycle, RxJava usage, Spark job management, CF configuration, HDFS/YARN integration, startup paths, build structure, and test conventions. Resolve duplicate U4/U5 scope and identify affected components.

Define interfaces, configuration properties, compatibility behavior, failure handling, persistence/retrieval flow, Spark termination semantics, test seams, and integration points for the implementable stories.

Implement the flexible RxJava module as a processor using the existing module extension model, including configuration, lifecycle handling, backpressure or subscription behavior as applicable, error propagation, and logging.
Add unit and component-level tests covering normal processing, configuration variants, asynchronous behavior, errors, shutdown, and compatibility with the existing module framework.

Review available customer use cases, assess ACL models and authorization boundaries, select an approach compatible with the XD runtime, define likely DSL and UI scope, and document phased next steps, alternatives, and open issues.

Create reproducible startup scenarios for admin and container servers, capture profiles, identify CPU bottlenecks, validate significant findings, document likely causes, and list pros and cons of candidate remedies.

Implement HDFS-backed storage and retrieval for custom module uber-jars, including path creation, stream handling, overwrite/version behavior, atomic upload strategy, missing/corrupt artifact handling, and integration with reinstall/failure recovery flows.

Add CF-user-configurable overrides for the HDFS storage location and YARN configuration location, including default resolution, validation, precedence rules, startup wiring, and backward compatibility.

Add the option to stop an existing managed Spark job, integrate it with the current job lifecycle and cleanup flow, handle already-completed or missing jobs, and provide appropriate status and error reporting.

Run and extend end-to-end or component integration tests for HDFS storage and reinstall, configuration overrides, Spark termination, module processing, startup-related behavior, and existing functionality regression.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, code review, and final delivery
activities.activity_description: Document configuration and operational behavior, record ACL spike and profiling outputs, update developer documentation, perform self-review and cleanup, resolve test findings, and prepare the increment for delivery.
